environmentBasis:
device=pengchengdemac-mini
os=macOS 26.5 (25F71) darwin-arm64
openvpn=OpenVPN Connect 3.8.1 (5790)
shadowrocket=Shadowrocket 2.2.90 (3378)
intranet=git.lifepilot.xyz
public=www.google.com

result.reason: OpenVPN alone reached git.lifepilot.xyz at 10.1.3.3 over utun with a matching TLS certificate. Shadowrocket alone reached www.google.com through its local proxy with a matching certificate, while DNS stayed in 198.18.0.0/15. Running both clients, in either order, removed the intranet route and enterprise DNS. Reconnecting OpenVPN did not restore them. The owner selected controlled rotation rather than simultaneous use.

observations.detail: git.lifepilot.xyz resolved to 10.1.3.3 via 10.1.3.1, routed utun15 gateway 10.0.23.13, TLS certificate included git.lifepilot.xyz. www.google.com timed out and the Shadowrocket proxy was closed.
Shadowrocket replaced the tunnel with 198.18.0.1. Intranet DNS became 198.18.0.30, enterprise DNS 10.1.3.1 was unreachable, and direct TLS to 10.1.3.3 failed. The public proxy returned HTTP 503.
OpenVPN reported connected, but no 10.0.23 tunnel remained. Intranet still resolved only inside 198.18.0.0/15 and the public proxy still returned HTTP 503.
www.google.com completed TLS through 127.0.0.1:1082 and presented a www.google.com certificate. System DNS for both names stayed in 198.18.0.0/15, so the route itself is not counted as a passed path.
OpenVPN reported connected, but the only tunnel address was 198.18.0.1. Enterprise DNS stayed unreachable. The public proxy still presented a www.google.com certificate.
Reconnecting OpenVPN did not create a 10.0.23 route or restore enterprise DNS. The public proxy remained healthy.
